subject: design-technology
title: Production Scales: Bespoke to Mass
welcome_lead: From one-off to a million units — different processes for different volumes.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: scales of production and matching processes.

concepts.def: Limited number of identical units in a single run.
Continuous large-volume production using a flow line.
24/7 large-scale process (oil refinery, glass float line).
Per-unit cost falls as production volume rises.
Fixed cost of preparing tooling for a production run.

walkthroughs.body_html: Bespoke: Savile Row suit. Batch: 100 wedding cakes. Mass: iPhones (~200m/year). Continuous: float glass, refinery output.
Higher-volume processes (injection moulding, die-casting) carry high setup costs (tooling £50k+) but low per-unit costs. Low-volume processes (machining, 3D printing) reverse this.
Selecting the right process means matching expected volume to setup vs unit-cost economics, alongside accuracy, surface finish and material properties.
